title: CLI fails to match files on Windows-style backslash paths
description:
On Windows, running the CLI with a backslash-style path (e.g. .\tests\fixtures\mastermind-ls\parts\footer.html) fails with "No matching .html or .php files found for: ..." even though the file exists.

Root cause: src/cli.js:66 passes raw argv patterns directly into fast-glob (fg). fast-glob treats backslash as a glob escape character, not a path separator, so a pattern like .\tests\fixtures\mastermind-ls\parts\footer.html gets mangled into .\tests\fixturesmastermind-lsparts\footer.html (backslash + following char is consumed as an escape sequence) and never matches.

Repro (confirmed):
- fg([".\\tests\\fixtures\\mastermind-ls\\parts\\footer.html"]) -> []
- fg(["./tests/fixtures/mastermind-ls/parts/footer.html"]) -> matches correctly

Reported via: `npm start .\tests\fixtures\mastermind-ls\parts\footer.html` and `npx . .\tests\fixtures\mastermind-ls\parts\footer.html` both failing.

Suggested fix: normalize backslashes to forward slashes on each pattern before passing to fast-glob in src/cli.js, so Windows-style paths are supported.

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** CLI fails to match files when given Windows-style backslash paths

**Current behavior:**
When a user passes a file pattern using Windows-style backslashes (e.g.
`.\tests\fixtures\mastermind-ls\parts\footer.html`) as a CLI argument, the
CLI reports "No matching .html or .php files found" even though the file
exists. This happens because the glob library used to resolve patterns
treats backslash as an escape character, not a path separator, so
backslash-delimited patterns are silently mangled and never match. This
affects `.\`, `..\`, and any other pattern using `\` as a separator, on
Windows only.

**Desired behavior:**
On Windows, file patterns using backslash separators resolve correctly and
match the same files their forward-slash equivalent would, with no manual
conversion required from the user. On non-Windows platforms, backslash
handling is unchanged (it retains its glob-escape meaning there).

**Key interfaces:**
- The function that turns CLI argv into glob patterns should normalize
  path separators (`\` → `/`) per pattern before handing them to the glob
  resolver, but only when running on Windows (`process.platform ===
  'win32'`). Do not normalize on other platforms — backslash is a legal
  filename character and glob-escape character there.
- No change to the glob resolver's matching semantics or its output shape
  (array of matched file paths) is needed.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] On Windows, a pattern like `.\tests\fixtures\mastermind-ls\parts\footer.html`
      resolves to the same file(s) as `./tests/fixtures/mastermind-ls/parts/footer.html`
- [ ] Existing forward-slash pattern behavior is unchanged on all platforms
- [ ] A new test passes a raw backslash-style pattern as CLI argv (not
      routed through any existing test helper that pre-normalizes
      separators) and asserts a match on Windows
- [ ] On non-Windows platforms, patterns containing `\` are passed through
      unmodified, preserving glob-escape semantics

**Out of scope:**
- Changing the existing fixture-path test helper that pre-normalizes
  separators for other tests — it serves a different purpose (portable
  fixture paths) and should stay as-is
- Any other cross-platform path handling issues not related to glob
  pattern matching
